title: Charlie Creath's four-piece band at the Kahoken Roadhouse
summary: After leaving Benbow in St. Louis he played an after-hours roadhouse with trumpeter Creath for $25 a week plus tips.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Let's talk about some of your work with people like Charlie Creath and Wilbur Sweatman. You played with Charlie Creath apparently in St. Louis.

Well, after I quit the show, Benbow's... I quit Benbow I think it was in St. Louis, Missouri. And I stayed there a while, and I got a chance to work with this trumpet player named Charlie Creath at a place called the Kahoken(?) Roadhouse. That's out...

That was an after-hour place. This guy who had the band... It was Charlie Creath; I think we had four pieces. It was an after-hour place, that started... It started, I'd say, about ten o'clock at night, and it would go on until five or six the next morning. I made twenty-five dollars a week, and the tips was very good. You could come out of there sometimes with fifteen or twenty dollars a piece in tips. Sometimes I'd make around fifty or sixty dollars a week.
That was pretty good. Charlie Creath played what instrument?
He was a trumpeter. He played trumpet.
Okay. And did he compose any music?
Not that I know of. He didn't... No, he didn't compose. No. During that time... I was kind of young then.
About what was the size of his band?
In St. Louis, yes. About how many musicians were there?
Yes. Trumpet, violin, piano and drums.
I see. Do you remember who the other musicians were?
The violin player? The piano player?
He was pretty well known then in the St. Louis area.
About how old a man was he when you were playing with him? This would be about 192_...
It must have been around 19... He must have been, say, around... I'd say '25. About 25 years old.
At the time that you were playing with him.
So he was a little younger than you.
